questions.question: What proves that a collaborative merge strategy converges?
options: Replicas that receive the same accepted changes end in the same valid state
Every edit reaches the server in under 100 milliseconds
The system uses WebSocket instead of HTTP
Only one participant can edit at a time
questions.explanation: Convergence is about equal final state after the same accepted changes arrive. Fast transport improves feedback but does not establish this property.

questions.question: Why are raw character offsets unsafe for concurrent inserts without transformation or stable merge rules?
options: Applying the same offsets in different arrival orders can produce different text
Offsets cannot be encoded as numbers
WebSocket automatically changes every offset
Text edits never occur concurrently
questions.explanation: An offset describes a position in one document state. Concurrent edits change that state, so arrival order can change what the offset means.

questions.question: A room has 10 active editors. Together they produce 1 durable change per second, each encoded as 200 bytes. Assuming each change is sent once to every other editor, what is the durable application-payload egress?
options: 200 bytes/s
1,800 bytes/s
2,000 bytes/s
20,000 bytes/s
questions.explanation: Each change has 9 recipients, so 1 change/s x 9 recipients x 200 bytes = 1,800 bytes/s. Protocol overhead and retries are outside this envelope.

questions.question: Why should cursor and typing awareness be handled separately from durable document changes?
options: Awareness can expire or be coalesced, while accepted document changes must survive reconnect and recovery
Awareness always requires stronger durability than document content
Presence must be replayed from the beginning of the document
Separate streams remove the need for authorization
questions.explanation: Presence describes the current session and may become stale. Durable changes represent user work and need stronger identity, persistence, and recovery guarantees.

questions.question: What should a reconnecting client exchange before resuming live updates?
options: Only its cursor color
A progress marker such as a version, sequence, state vector, or sync message
A new wall-clock timestamp that overwrites every remote change
The full awareness history for every former participant
questions.explanation: Progress metadata lets peers determine which durable changes are missing and whether a delta or checkpoint is required.

questions.question: A CRDT makes replicas converge, but two users concurrently assign different owners to a task that may have only one owner. What remains an application responsibility?
options: Define and enforce the single-owner invariant and surface any unresolved semantic conflict
Replace stable operation IDs with client wall clocks
Persist cursor updates forever
Disable authentication because merge is deterministic
questions.explanation: Datatype convergence does not decide every business rule. The application must validate domain invariants and give users an honest resolution path.
